ranking.note: Base of the Chain-over-IPC chain: standalone crash hardening that #29409 and #10102 build on, so it is worth a reviewer first.
Kept P1 as the category-defining PR, but placed after the two prerequisites it is stacked on.
Raised to P1: same class of IPC event-loop use-after-free/termination as #35932 and #36520, which are P1.
Moved up: it changes mining IPC call mechanics (cancellation via promises) per agreed RFC #33575, affecting external consumers' interface stability more than the other P2s.
Raised to P2 for consistency with #36105: both are wrapper breakages on real install targets, and this one makes the wrapper fail outright on common distro layouts.

inconsistencies: Overlapping work: #32387 (ipc: add windows support) states it also fixes the Windows wrapper to await child processes, which is exactly what #36105 does standalone. Review #36105 first and have #32387 rebase on it rather than carrying a duplicate fix.

Dependency chain whose order matters: #36520 -> #29409 -> #10102 -> #19460 -> #19461. The later ones cannot land or be meaningfully evaluated before the earlier ones; reviewing bottom-up is the only productive order.
#36190 is pure test coverage for the behaviour introduced by #36105; it is not reviewable independently and should follow #36105.

#35932 and #36572 both address lifetime/teardown races in the same IPC event-loop and disconnect path (both touch or depend on libmultiprocess disconnect fixes). They should be looked at together to avoid conflicting fixes.

#36597 is a wallet-interface signature change whose only stated consumer is an out-of-process GUI; by the category scope it is wallet-first and only marginally ipc, which is why it sits at the top of P3 rather than among the interface-mechanics PRs.

#30437 (bitcoin-mine client) and #36192 (IPC createNewBlock error-path test) both exercise the mining interface from outside the node; #30437 provides the harness and is the more consequential of the two.
result.notes: The band spread is driven by the category's stated priorities: crash/disconnect correctness across the process boundary and the prerequisites of the process-separation stack form P1; platform coverage, mining-interface mechanics and the per-executable -ipcconnect work form P2; test, fuzz and build-check additions without a blocked consumer stay P3. No P4 was warranted: every PR here has a concrete consumer or a named issue.
